observation.visible_scene: An extreme macro close-up of a single open human eye: a vivid blue iris with a dark round pupil, brown eyelashes and lids, and a pale sclera on the right crossed by red capillaries. A reflection of small glowing dots (yellow, green, cyan) sits on the wet cornea like a distant horizon of lights. The framing keeps the eye centered and fills the screen throughout.
visible_changes: The reflected band of lights drifts downward across the eye's surface: in the early frames it lies across the middle/lower iris, while by the later frames it has moved to the bottom edge of the pupil.
As it moves, the dot-cluster stretches into a thin horizontal streak, with a green flare extending to the left over the iris and a brighter white-yellow flare extending to the right over the sclera.
The individual points of light flicker and change brightness between frames, giving a shimmering quality to the reflection.
The eye stays open the whole time; the lids do not close and no blink occurs.
The pupil and iris remain roughly the same size and position, with no clear dilation or constriction.
The overall composition (eye position, scale) is largely steady, with at most a very slight shift.
outside_clip_unknowns: What the reflected lights actually are (a cityscape, a screen, a street) is not resolved within the clip, nor is the light source that produces the reflection.
Whether the downward drift of the reflection is caused by eye movement, head/camera movement, or a moving light source is not determinable from this excerpt.
Events before the first frame and after the last frame are unknown.
uncertain_details: The exact cause of the reflection's motion (saccade vs. camera vs. light-source movement) is uncertain.
Any minor camera drift or zoom is hard to confirm because the eye fills the frame and there is little separate background evidence.
The apparent texture shimmer in the iris may be a lighting/reflection effect rather than physical change.
